North Quays
Forbairt Eacnamaíoch / Economic Development
Works are progressing well on the North Quays main contract. For the Sustainable Transport Bridge the second of four 
cofferdams is currently being constructed. This will allow for water to be drained from within the cofferdams, creating a 
workspace below water level and permit construction of the concrete pier foundations.        
Piling and laying of foundations at the existing bus station, new train station and bridge structures are also ongoing and 
progressing well. 
Traffi c management measures are in place along Dock Road and operating well.  A new road surface and paving are 
being installed in the current works area and the same process, installing sewer and surface water network services 
followed by resurfacing and paving will then progress to the next section of Dock Road and accompanied by associated 
traffi c management measures.  
ROD Consulting Engineers have been appointed as Design Consultants for the Flood Defence contract.  
David Walsh Civil Engineering contractor is progressing on programme for both the Pump Station Enabling Works and 
the Ferrybank Pump Station relocation contract.

Management Report Plenary 12th October 2023.
TOURISM 
A delegation from Märkischer Kreis, Germany, will arrive to Waterford on the 15th October. Waterford formed a twinning 
partnership with the German region earlier in the year. During their visit the team will experience some of what Water-
ford has to offer in the way of tourism, education, history & heritage as they travel across the county. We look forward to 
welcoming the Märkischer Kreis delegates to Waterford and to continue strengthening the relationship with our Europe-
an counterparts.
The next Economic Development & Enterprise SPC is scheduled on December 13th 2023.

Decade of Commemorations- All districts:
The fi nal conference of the Waterford Decade of Centenaries Programme takes place in the Large Room of City Hall on 
Saturday 21st October 9am-4pm. Attendance is free of charge but pre-registration is required on Eventbrite https://bit.
ly/3Ro8eDE. 
A Screening of the Dying Days fi lm on the death of Liam Lynch and the end of the Civil War took place to a full 
auditorium at Garter Lane Theatre on Thursday 28th September at 7pm opened by Mayor Joe Conway.
A talk commemorating the centenary of the election of Caitlín Brugha   the wife of Cathal Brugha in 1923 took place on 
September 19th in Dungarvan Library and was attended by a grandson of Caitlín Brugha.  
Landscape Forum:
A National Landscape Forum took place at Mount Congreve on September 28th and 20th discussing the National 
Landscape Strategy and issues of landscape past and landscape future. 
Woodstown Viking Site:
Archaeologists from the Discovery Programme will complete a geo-physical survey of the Woodstown Viking Site in 
early October. A delegation from Stavangar Museum in Norway is planning a visit Waterford in early November 10th 
taking in City Hall, the Viking Triangle, Waterford Museums and the Woodstown Viking site.

PRIDE OF PLACE:
The National Pride of Place awards event is taking place in Armagh on November 10th where CAPE-ability Lismore 
(winners of the overall PPN award) and the Larchville Lisduggan Residents Group (nominated by the Housing Dept.) will 
be present.
MIGRANT INTEGRATION:
The last Migrant Integration Strategy Meeting took place on the 13th September 2023 and the next meeting is sched-
uled to take place on the 1st November 2023.  Each Local Authority in the Country are establishing “Local Authority 
Integration Teams” and recruitment for a number of positions for this team is currently underway. Discussions also took 
place around the review of the Migrant Integration Strategy Subgroup and Migrant Integration Forum.
SICAP
Work in ongoing with Waterford Area Partnership continuing to implement the SICAP programme on behalf of the 
LCDC. SICAP Budget allocations for 2023 have now been confirmed and the budget for Waterford City & County (24-1) 
is €1,319,399 excluding the Ukrainian budget allocation which has been set as €232,758 by the Department. 
The 2023 Mid-year review process is complete with no issues identified.
Planning for the new SICAP 2024+ programme has now commenced with the tender process underway.
UKRAINIAN COMMUNITY RESPONSE FORUM:
The Ukrainian CRF is in place to assist with housing, supporting and integrating Ukrainian refugees into our 
communities.   All key agencies are working in collaboration to provide services and supports to all Ukrainians arriving 
into Waterford. Approximately 2,500 Ukrainian refugees have been registered in Waterford to date with over 1,891 
#Ukrainians having been received directly into Waterford Council run Rest Centres in Dungarvan and Waterford City.  To 
date 1,382 have been matched with pledged and other accommodation sourced by Waterford Council.   Over 90% of 
expiring licence agreements are being renewed and the team continue to work on supporting pledge owners and 
occupiers here in Waterford. Waterford Area Partnership are supporting all of those who have moved with integration 
into our communities. The  ‘offer a home’ pledge call for vacant properties is still open with over 240 Ukrainians being 
accommodated in pledged accommodation  to date.  Any queries on same should be directed to 
offerahome@waterfordcouncil.ie or 058 22059.   
WLCSP MEETINGS:
The Chair, and or CoOrdinator held meetings with The Probation Service, TUSLA, Age Friendly Implementation Group, 
Slaintecare Local Implementation Team, and WWETB. The CoOrdinator presented at The Southern Regional 
Networking Event for Joint Policing Committees, on behalf of the Partnership The Education, Training & Awareness and 
Building Community Capacity Working Group met on the 3rd October 2023 and the Reducing Criminality and Safe 
Environment & Infrastructure Working Group, met on 21st September The WLCSP Plenary Meeting took place on 
Tuesday 26th September 2023, and Assistant Garda Commissioner Hilman presented to the Partnership, with a 
representative from the Policing Authority present. The Agenda included an update on implementation of the Community 
Safety Plan, Quarterly Reports from the Partners, the new Garda Divisional Structure and Emerging areas of concern 
which included ASP, Organised City Centre begging, drug availability West Waterford and Halloween safety 
preparations.
SCARY BUT SAFE HALLOWEEN PILOT:
The partnership are currently implementing the ‘Scary but Safe Halloween’ pilot community safety event which will incop-
rporate a successful Creative Ireland application for a creative community led event called ‘The Hill at Halloween’, based 
in Ballybricked with the bandstand as the focal point.  
LCSP SMALL GRANT FUND
The Department of Justice have approved a Waterford Community Safety Partnership Small Grants Fund to deliver 
innovative projects and initiatives that respond to the needs identified in the WLCSP Community Safety Plan 2023-2028. 
The object of the grants is to stimulate and nourish local community safety initiatives related to the actions within the 
Community Safety Plan. The grants will be announced by local paper, radio, and a social media campaign with amounts 
of €1,000 to €5,000 available to a total of €50,000. Applications will open from 6th October to 20th October, with grant 
amount awarded and allocated by 17th November to be expended by 31st December. Please ensure that any suitable 
projects within the communities and organisations that you represent are informed of the grant being launched next 
week

CLIMATE ACTION
Climate Action Plan Draft to launch on 25th October
The consultation period for the Draft Climate Action Plan will open on 25th October and will stay open for 6 weeks. The 
Climate Action Team will host a number of events in the city as part of the Imagine Festival to encourage the public to 
contribute to the Plan. The Climate Action Team will also hold events in libraries and in GAA grounds across the county 
to meet people where they are.
Bioenergy opportunities for Waterford – Biobus to visit
The Biobus is a Science Foundation Ireland project, a bus with exhibitions around bioenergy (energy from derived from 
natural material such as grass and husks). Members of the public are welcome to visit the bus in John Robert’s Square 
on 22nd October and in An Rinn on 12th November.
Rates Energy Discount Scheme
The Deadline for submissions for the Commercial Energy Rates Discount is 29th September. As of today, 550 businesses 
have availed of the discount in exchange for energy saving actions.

ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION & AWARENESS
Waste Prevention
During October there is a focus on Circular Economy living. An emphasis will be placed on repair and reuse during this 
month, including the launch of a basic DIY toolkit that can be borrowed from the libraries. In addition to this, we will be 
holding a clothes swap event and a textile exhibition in Central Library.
Schools
The Tom Murphy Litter Challenge for Secondary Schools has been launched in Waterford city and county. All 
secondary schools were invited to enter the competition and entrants will receive litter pickers, high visibility vests, 
gloves and bags to enable them to carry out litter picks of their designated area. These clean ups will take place during 
October and November. The prizegiving and presentation of certificates of participation will take place in the Mayors 
Parlour in early December. Tom Murphy Car Sales have sponsored the prize fund of €1,500 for the winning school.
Composting for Schools Programme
8 Secondary Schools are also taking part in the Composting for Schools programme, which involves 2 visits to the 
schools to carry out a waste audit to help schools to prevent, reduce and reuse their waste. There is a strong focus on 
food waste. Schools can also take part in 5 online sessions to learn more about waste prevention, recycling and com-
posting within a school.
Green Schools Programme
The Green Schools programme for the new school year is well under way now. Along with schools visits, there have 
been webinars for Primary Schools and Secondary schools in Co. Waterford. These were held for each theme of the 
programme e.g. waste, litter, water, biodiversity, travel, etc and took place on line in the evening. These webinars are 
designed to support secondary school teachers and students as they work through their current theme.  The majority of 
teachers found online seminars to be a convenient way to learn about their current Green Schools theme as it elim-
inates travel time to and from the seminar. The Environmental Awareness Officer will be available to visit schools or 
answer any questions that they might have.
Community Clean-Ups
Waterford City & County Council facilitates community clean ups throughout the year to clean up litter and illegally 
dumped waste from approach roads, local beauty spots, beaches and general public areas. The Environment 
Department continue to supply bags, gloves and litter pickers from both Dungarvan and Waterford offices to many of the 
groups taking part, as well as collecting the bags of litter afterwards.

7-day extension to the Slurry Spreading Period
In light of the recent wet period of weather and considering the scientific criteria to determine whether the period for 
slurry spreading can be extended beyond the 30th September, Darragh O’Brien T.D, Minister for Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage, in consultation with Charlie McConalogue T.D, Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine, 
has agreed to extend the slurry spreading period by 7 days. This is in line with the maximum period that can be granted 
at present based on the published criteria.
The closed period for slurry spreading will therefore commence on the 8th October 2023. Announcing the decision, 
Minister McConalogue stated: “I recognise that unseasonable weather conditions experienced this summer and within 
the last week, have impacted trafficability and provided limited opportunities for possible slurry applications by farmers 
and contractors.”
Minister McConalogue pointed out: “Slurry is a valuable source of nutrients and is best utilised using low emission slurry 
spreading and especially in spring when growth and weather conditions are typically favourable for utilising nutrients 
and limit run-off and emissions to the environment.”
The Minister added, “The majority of slurry has been spread well in advance of the closed period and this must be 
acknowledged and indeed commended. This limited extension will allow farmers spread any remaining slurry in the best 
conditions available to them.”
Given the need to deliver on our commitments to improving water quality, it is fundamental slurry is applied under the 
right conditions and at the right time of year. It is critical that farm practices deliver on water quality. Farmers are 
reminded to observe Buffer Zones that apply at this time of the year.
This decision has been made in accordance with the provisions set out in Article 19 (1) of SI No. 113 of 2022 (as 
amended).
